passages.text: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
passages.sermon: Phoebe is our sister.\r\nPhoebe serves as a deacon of the church in Cenchrea.\r\nI commend Phoebe to you.
passages.original: Συνίστημι δὲ ὑμῖν Φοίβην τὴν ἀδελφὴν ἡμῶν οὖσαν καὶ διάκονον τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἐν Κενχρεαῖς

passages.text: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.
passages.sermon:
Phoebe is our sister.
Phoebe serves the church in Cenchrea.
Welcome Phoebe in the Lord.
Welcome her as you would welcome the saints.
Help her with anything she needs from you.
Phoebe has helped many people.
Phoebe has also helped me.
passages.original: ἵνα αὐτὴν προσδέξησθε ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀξίως τῶν ἁγίων καὶ παραστῆτε αὐτῇ ἐν ᾧ ἂν ὑμῶν χρῄζῃ πράγματι καὶ γὰρ αὐτὴ προστάτις πολλῶν ἐγενήθη καὶ ἐμοῦ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.
passages.sermon:
Prisca and Aquila are my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.
They have risked their lives for me.
Greet Prisca and Aquila.
I am grateful to them.
All the churches of the Gentiles are also grateful to them.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν τοὺς συνεργούς μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ οἵτινες ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς μου τὸν ἑαυτῶν τράχηλον ὑπέθηκαν οἷς οὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος εὐχαριστῶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσαι αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῶν ἐθνῶν

passages.text: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
passages.sermon:
Prisca and Aquila host a church in their house.
Greet the church that meets in their house.
Epenetus is my beloved friend.
Epenetus was the first person in the province of Asia to believe in Christ.
Greet Epenetus.
passages.original: καὶ τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίαν Ἀσπάσασθε Ἐπαίνετον τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου ὅς ἐστιν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀσίας εἰς Χριστόν

passages.text: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
passages.sermon: Mary is a woman who has served the church in Rome.\r\nShe has worked very hard for the believers there.\r\nGreet Mary.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Μαριάν ἥτις πολλὰ ἐκοπίασεν εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
passages.sermon:
Andronicus and Junia are my fellow countrymen.
They are also my fellow prisoners.
Greet Andronicus and Junia.
They are outstanding among the apostles.
They were in Christ before I was.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ἀνδρόνικον καὶ Ἰουνίαν τοὺς συγγενεῖς μου καὶ συναιχμαλώτους μου οἵτινές εἰσιν ἐπίσημοι ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις οἳ καὶ πρὸ ἐμοῦ γέγοναν ἐν Χριστῷ

passages.text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
passages.sermon: Ampliatus is my beloved in the Lord.\r\nGreet Ampliatus.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ἀμπλιᾶτον τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
passages.sermon:
Urbanus is our fellow worker in Christ.
Greet Urbanus.
Stachys is my beloved.
Greet Stachys.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Οὐρβανὸν τὸν συνεργὸν ἡμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ Στάχυν τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου

passages.text: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
passages.sermon: Apelles is approved in Christ.\r\nGreet Apelles.\r\nGreet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ἀπελλῆν τὸν δόκιμον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐκ τῶν Ἀριστοβούλου

passages.text: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman. Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Herodion is my fellow countryman.
Greet Herodion.
Some people belong to the household of Narcissus.
These people are in the Lord.
Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ἡρῳδίωνα τὸν συγγενῆ μου Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐκ τῶν Ναρκίσσου τοὺς ὄντας ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Tryphena and Tryphosa are women.
They have worked hard in the Lord.
Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa.
Persis is my beloved.
She has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Persis.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Τρύφαιναν καὶ Τρυφῶσαν τὰς κοπιώσας ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἀσπάσασθε Περσίδα τὴν ἀγαπητήν ἥτις πολλὰ ἐκοπίασεν ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
passages.sermon:
Rufus is chosen in the Lord.
Greet Rufus.
Greet his mother.
His mother has also been a mother to me.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ῥοῦφον τὸν ἐκλεκτὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Rome.
He gives instructions to greet certain believers.
Greet Asyncritus.
Greet Phlegon.
Greet Hermes.
Greet Patrobas.
Greet Hermas.
Greet the brothers who are with them.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Ἀσύνκριτον Φλέγοντα Ἑρμῆν Πατρόβαν Ἑρμᾶν καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς ἀδελφούς

passages.text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Rome.
He tells them to greet Philologus.
He tells them to greet Julia.
He tells them to greet Nereus.
He tells them to greet the sister of Nereus.
He tells them to greet Olympas.
He tells them to greet all the saints who are with these people.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε Φιλόλογον καὶ Ἰουλίαν Νηρέα καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ὀλυμπᾶν καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς πάντας ἁγίους

passages.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Rome.
He tells them to greet one another.
He says to use a holy kiss when they greet each other.
All the churches that belong to Christ send their greetings to the believers in Rome.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι πᾶσαι τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Rome.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul urges them to be careful.
Some people create divisions.
Some people cause obstacles.
These divisions and obstacles go against the teaching the Christians learned.
Paul tells the Christians to watch out for such people.
Paul tells the Christians to turn away from them.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί σκοπεῖν τοὺς τὰς διχοστασίας καὶ τὰ σκάνδαλα παρὰ τὴν διδαχὴν ἣν ὑμεῖς ἐμάθετε ποιοῦντας καὶ ἐκκλίνετε ἀπ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
passages.sermon:
Some people do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ.
These people serve only their own desires.
They use smooth talk.
They use flattery.
They deceive the hearts of innocent people.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Χριστῷ οὐ δουλεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τῇ ἑαυτῶν κοιλίᾳ καὶ διὰ τῆς χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐλογίας ἐξαπατῶσιν τὰς καρδίας τῶν ἀκάκων

passages.text: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Christians in Rome.
Paul saw that these Christians obeyed God.
Everyone heard about their obedience.
Paul felt joy because of their obedience.
Paul wanted them to be wise about what is good.
Paul wanted them to be innocent about what is evil.
passages.original: Ἡ γὰρ ὑμῶν ὑπακοὴ εἰς πάντας ἀφίκετο ἐφ’ ὑμῖν οὖν χαίρω θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς σοφοὺς εἶναι εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν ἀκεραίους δὲ εἰς τὸ κακόν

passages.text: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of peace.
God will soon crush Satan.
God will crush Satan under your feet.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ is with you.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης συντρίψει τὸν Σατανᾶν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ὑμῶν ἐν τάχει Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.
passages.sermon:
Timothy sends you greetings.
Timothy is my fellow worker.
Lucius sends you greetings.
Jason sends you greetings.
Sosipater sends you greetings.
Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater are my fellow countrymen.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Τιμόθεος ὁ συνεργός μου καὶ Λούκιος καὶ Ἰάσων καὶ Σωσίπατρος οἱ συγγενεῖς μου

passages.text: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
passages.sermon: Tertius wrote down this letter.\r\nTertius greets you.\r\nTertius greets you in the Lord.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζομαι ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ Τέρτιος ὁ γράψας τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings. Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.
passages.sermon:
Gaius sends you greetings.
Gaius has hosted me.
Gaius has also hosted the whole church.
Erastus sends you greetings.
Erastus is the city treasurer.
Quartus sends you greetings.
Quartus is our brother.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Γάϊος ὁ ξένος μου καὶ ὅλης τῆς ἐκκλησίας Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἔραστος ὁ οἰκονόμος τῆς πόλεως καὶ Κούαρτος ὁ ἀδελφός

passages.text: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith — to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is able to strengthen you.
God does this by my gospel.
God does this by the proclamation of Jesus Christ.
God revealed a mystery.
This mystery was hidden for ages.
Now God has revealed this mystery.
God made it known through the writings of the prophets.
God did this by the command of the eternal God.
God made this known to lead all nations to obedience that comes from faith.
God alone is wise.
Glory belongs to God forever.
God receives this glory through Jesus Christ.
Amen.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ ὑμᾶς στηρίξαι κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν μυστηρίου χρόνοις αἰωνίοις σεσιγημένου φανερωθέντος δὲ νῦν διά τε γραφῶν προφητικῶν κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ αἰωνίου Θεοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη γνωρισθέντος μόνῳ σοφῷ Θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν
